## Overview

Fixes the Qwen3.5 part of vllm-project/recipes#1156. On recipes.vllm.ai the command builder renders the selected hardware and variant. The guide below it is the same static text for every selection, yet the Qwen3.5 guides held commands for a single configuration:
- a "Docker" section that was only the Intel XPU image;
- launch commands for one GPU and checkpoint;
- a client example whose `model` only the BF16 variant serves.

Readers could not tell which instructions applied to them.

This keeps the guides to what holds for every configuration. Content that is specific to a configuration moves to `notes` and `troubleshooting`, which the builder filters by the current selection.

It also fixes Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, whose builder offered no NVIDIA or AMD GPU at all.

## Claims

**Guides (all eight Qwen3.5 recipes)**

- **Removed:** the install, `docker`, and `vllm serve` blocks. The builder renders each of them for the selected configuration.
- **Kept:**
  - hardware sizing;
  - AMD measurements and explanations;
  - the MXFP4 section;
  - long context;
  - references.
- **Converted to a table:** 397B's per-workload configurations (workload, hardware, checkpoint, parallelism, other settings). Each row now names the hardware it was verified on.
- **Client examples:** they read the served name from `/v1/models` (`client.models.list().data[0].id`), so they work for every variant. This includes the Ascend variants, which set `--served-model-name qwen3.5`.
- **Thinking toggle:** the hint now sits with the client example, both per request (`chat_template_kwargs`) and per server.

**Notes and troubleshooting**

- **Notes** (shown only for a matching selection):
  - Arc Pro validation settings, including `--max-model-len 8192`, for 9B, 27B and 35B-A3B;
  - "MTP on ROCm: use an FP8 KV cache" for 397B.
- **Troubleshooting:**
  - the Mamba cache assert, on NVIDIA and AMD;
  - experimental prefix caching;
  - the CPU startup timeout (35B-A3B);
  - Encoder Parallel memory (397B).

**4B and 35B-A3B hardware**

- **The bug:** vllm-project/recipes#1029 set each variant's `supported_hardware` from the recipe's `verified` hardware, which was Xeon 6 and Arc Pro only. `supported_hardware` is an allowlist, so every other GPU was locked out of these pages, and the default page opened on Arc Pro B60.
- **The fix:**
  - BF16 has no allowlist again, so it runs everywhere. Xeon 6 and Arc remain because `meta.hardware` declares them.
  - The quantized variants list `arch:sm90/sm100/sm103/gfx942/gfx950` plus the Arc Pro ids. They still exclude Xeon, which is what #1029 wanted.

## Validation

- **Renderer check:** `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes against recipes main. `test-schema`, `test-guide-html`, `test-context` and `test-overlay` pass.
- **Rendered commands:** built against recipes main before and after this change and compared every JSON rendering (`command`, `argv`, `env`, `docker_command`, `worker_commands`).
  - No existing per-hardware rendering changed.
  - The changes are additions: 380 new renderings (NVIDIA and AMD for 4B and 35B-A3B, plus their promoted variants).
  - The default-hardware files of 35B-A3B moved from Arc Pro B60 to H200.
  - Xeon 6 still renders only the BF16 variant.
- **Builder:** checked locally.
  - 9B on Arc Pro B60 shows the validation note.
  - The 397B guide renders the configuration table and the MXFP4 section.
- **vllm-ascend overlay:** the 397B overlay carries no guide sections, so the guide edit doesn't change it.

## Details

- **Overlap with #63881.** That PR rewrites the 35B-A3B CPU install block that this PR deletes. Whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. Otherwise #63881 can drop its `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.yaml` hunk.
- **Removed outright:**
  - the 397B AMD pip note (Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, glibc ≥ 2.35);
  - its "use `cu130-nightly` on Blackwell" line.

  The builder's install block covers both, and both had gone stale.
- **Not in this PR:** the same `supported_hardware` pattern from #1029 in the other recipes it touched (Gemma 4, Llama, Phi-4, Qwen3, …), and the other guides that still carry launch commands. Those are follow-ups.

   ## Overview
 
   [Qwen3.5](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model featuring a gated delta networks architecture with 397B total parameters and 17B active parameters. This guide covers how to efficiently deploy and serve the model across different hardware configurations and workload profiles using vLLM.
 
-  ## Prerequisites
-
-  ### Pip Install
-
-  #### NVIDIA
-  ```bash
-  uv venv
-  source .venv/bin/activate
-  uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend=auto
-  ```
-
-  #### AMD
-  > Note: The vLLM wheel for ROCm requires Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, and glibc >= 2.35. If your environment does not meet these requirements, please use the Docker-based setup. Supported GPUs: MI300X, MI325X, MI355X.
-  ```bash
-  uv venv --python 3.12
-  source .venv/bin/activate
-  uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm
-  ```
-
-  ### Docker
-
-  #### NVIDIA
-  ```bash
-  docker run --gpus all \
-    -p 8000:8000 \
-    --ipc=host \
-    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
-    vllm/vllm-openai Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B \
-      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-      --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-      --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-  For Blackwell GPUs, use `vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly`.
-
-  #### AMD
-  ```bash
-  docker run --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
-    --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
-    --group-add video \
-    --ipc=host \
-    -p 8000:8000 \
-    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
-    vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest \
-    Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ## Deployment Configurations
-
-  The configurations below have been verified on 8x H200 GPUs and 8x MI300X/MI355X GPUs. We recommend using the official FP8 checkpoint [Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8) for optimal serving efficiency.
-
-  ### Throughput-Focused (Text-Only)
-
-  For maximum text throughput under high concurrency, use `--language-model-only` to skip loading the vision encoder and free up memory for KV cache, and enable Expert Parallelism.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    -dp 8 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ### Throughput-Focused (Multimodal)
-
-  For multimodal workloads, use `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` for data-parallel vision encoding and `--mm-processor-cache-type shm` for shared-memory caching of preprocessed multimodal inputs.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    -dp 8 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
-    --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  To enable tool calling, add `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` to the serve command.
-
-  ### Latency-Focused
-
-  For latency-sensitive workloads at low concurrency, enable MTP-1 speculative decoding and disable prefix caching. MTP-1 reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) with a high acceptance rate, at the cost of lower throughput under load.
-
-  > Note (AMD): MTP runs on ROCm with vLLM 0.31.0 (verified with the single-GPU MXFP4 setup below). On ROCm,
-  > pair it with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`: with the default KV cache its speedup fades as the prompt grows.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3
-  ```
-
-  ### GB200 Deployment
-
-  We recommend using the NVFP4 checkpoint [nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4) for optimal serving efficiency on GB200 nodes.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
-    -dp 4 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ### MI355X Deployment
+  ## Verified configurations
 
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    -tp 2 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
+  These configurations were verified on 8x H200, 8x MI300X/MI355X and GB200. On
+  H200 and MI300X/MI355X they used the official FP8 checkpoint
+  [Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8).

This guide covers how to efficiently deploy and serve the model across different hardware configurations and workload profiles using vLLM.
 
-  ## Prerequisites
-
-  ### Pip Install
-

-  ```bash
-  uv venv
-  source .venv/bin/activate
-  uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend=auto
-  ```
-
-  #### AMD
-  > Note: The vLLM wheel for ROCm requires Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, and glibc >= 2.35. If your environment does not meet these requirements, please use the Docker-based setup. Supported GPUs: MI300X, MI325X, MI355X.
-  ```bash
-  uv venv --python 3.12
-  source .venv/bin/activate
-  uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm
-  ```
-
-  ### Docker
-
-  #### NVIDIA
-  ```bash
-  docker run --gpus all \
-    -p 8000:8000 \
-    --ipc=host \
-    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
-    vllm/vllm-openai Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B \
-      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-      --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-      --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-  For Blackwell GPUs, use `vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly`.
-
-  #### AMD
-  ```bash
-  docker run --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
-    --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
-    --group-add video \
-    --ipc=host \
-    -p 8000:8000 \
-    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
-    vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest \
-    Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ## Deployment Configurations
-
-  The configurations below have been verified on 8x H200 GPUs and 8x MI300X/MI355X GPUs. We recommend using the official FP8 checkpoint [Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8) for optimal serving efficiency.
-
-  ### Throughput-Focused (Text-Only)
-
-  For maximum text throughput under high concurrency, use `--language-model-only` to skip loading the vision encoder and free up memory for KV cache, and enable Expert Parallelism.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    -dp 8 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ### Throughput-Focused (Multimodal)
-
-  For multimodal workloads, use `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` for data-parallel vision encoding and `--mm-processor-cache-type shm` for shared-memory caching of preprocessed multimodal inputs.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
-    -dp 8 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
-    --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  To enable tool calling, add `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` to the serve command.

-
-  For latency-sensitive workloads at low concurrency, enable MTP-1 speculative decoding and disable prefix caching. MTP-1 reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) with a high acceptance rate, at the cost of lower throughput under load.

-    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
-    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3
-  ```
-
-  ### GB200 Deployment
-
-  We recommend using the NVFP4 checkpoint [nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4) for optimal serving efficiency on GB200 nodes.
-
-  ```bash
-  vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
-    -dp 4 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
-
-  ### MI355X Deployment
+  ## Verified configurations
 
-  ```bash

-    -tp 2 \
-    --enable-expert-parallel \
-    --language-model-only \
-    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
-    --enable-prefix-caching
-  ```
+  These configurations were verified on 8x H200, 8x MI300X/MI355X and GB200. On
